newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mixed in slow trading.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices were mixed on Monday amid subdued activity, millfeed brokers said.
Volatility in the CBOT grain markets appeared to have little impact on millfeed values, dealers said.
"It is dead quiet," a Kansas dealer said. "I think the significance in this market is what the mills will be doing this week and nobody knows that yet."
"There has not been enough time to analyze it," a North Carolina dealer said, referring to the drop in soybeans. He noted that nearby production of flour remained low and runtimes have not been good.
"I would say demand is coming mainly from merchants trying to cover shorts. I do not see any new sales being made other than fill-in orders," the North Carolina dealer said.

Chicago Board of Trade soybean new crop futures tumbled on the U.S. Department of Agriculture's soybean acreage estimate which put 1997 soybean plantings at 68.8 million acres, the highest since 1980 and well above trade expectations for 65.85 million.
